items.stem: Compare sensory memory, short-term memory and long-term memory.
items.answer: Sensory – large capacity, less than a second; STM – about 7 items, brief, acoustic; LTM – unlimited, permanent, semantic.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Sensory – large capacity, less than a second; STM – about 7 items, brief, acoustic; LTM – unlimited, permanent, semantic.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about knowledge representation, constructive memory and forgetting is NOT correct?
items.answer: According to Ebbinghaus, forgetting is slow at first and rapid later.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Forgetting is rapid at first and slows down later.
options: Bartlett showed that people change material while recalling it to fit their schemas.
According to Ebbinghaus, forgetting is slow at first and rapid later.
Memory is not a copy of the past but a reconstruction.
Interference theory explains forgetting by competition between different learnings.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Kavya remembers a 10-digit number as 98-765-43-210 instead of ten separate digits. Identify the memory strategy illustrated.
items.answer: Chunking.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: chunking.

items.stem: What is meant by 'explicit memory' in the context of levels of processing and types of long-term memory?
items.answer: Memory that is consciously and deliberately recalled.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: explicit memory correctly explained as memory that is consciously and deliberately recalled.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'storage' and 'retrieval'.
items.answer: Storage: the stage of memory in which encoded information is retained over a period of time. Retrieval: the stage of memory in which stored information is brought out for use.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'storage' (the stage of memory in which encoded information is retained over a period of time.) and 1 mark for 'retrieval' (the stage of memory in which stored information is brought out for use.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.stem: Read the case and answer. Before reading a chapter, Anil skims it, writes questions, reads to answer them, recites the answers and then tests himself. Name the study method shown here and explain it briefly.
items.answer: PQRST method: Preview, Question, Read, Self-recitation and Test improve study and retention.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for naming it (PQRST method); 1 mark for the explanation (Preview, Question, Read, Self-recitation and Test improve study and retention).

items.stem:
Statement: Chunking improves short-term memory.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Grouping items into meaningful units allows more information to be held within its limited capacity.
items.markingKey: (d) Grouping items into meaningful units allows more information to be held within its limited capacity.
options: Short-term memory was found to be not a single store but a system that also processes information.
Information in short-term memory fades quickly unless it is rehearsed.
Each item is linked to a familiar location that serves as a retrieval cue.
Grouping items into meaningful units allows more information to be held within its limited capacity.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on knowledge representation, constructive memory and forgetting and answer the questions that follow.
"Bartlett showed that people change material while recalling it to fit their schemas. Memory is not a copy of the past but a reconstruction. Knowledge in long-term memory is organised in the form of concepts, categories and schemas."
(i) According to Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve, forgetting is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'retroactive interference' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Studying similar subjects one after another may lead to forgetting. (2)
items.answer: (i) rapid at first and then slows down (ii) Interference in which later learning interferes with the recall of earlier learning. (iii) Similar learnings interfere with each other.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) rapid at first and then slows down (ii) Interference in which later learning interferes with the recall of earlier learning. (iii) Similar learnings interfere with each other.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: We cannot easily explain how we ride a bicycle.
items.answer: Procedural memory stores skills that are not easily put into words.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: Procedural memory stores skills that are not easily put into words. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem: The following statement about nature of memory: encoding, storage and retrieval is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Retrieval is the first stage of memory."
items.answer: Encoding is the first stage; retrieval is the last.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (Encoding is the first stage; retrieval is the last.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about knowledge representation, constructive memory and forgetting is correct?
items.answer: Memory is not a copy of the past but a reconstruction.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: Bartlett showed memory is a constructive process. That is retroactive interference; proactive is old learning disrupting new learning. Forgetting is rapid at first and slows down later.
options: Memory is an exact copy of past events.
Proactive interference is when new learning disrupts old learning.
Memory is not a copy of the past but a reconstruction.
According to Ebbinghaus, forgetting is slow at first and rapid later.

items.stem: What is meant by 'method of loci' in the context of enhancing memory?
items.answer: A mnemonic in which items are placed as images in familiar locations in a known order.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: method of loci correctly explained as a mnemonic in which items are placed as images in familiar locations in a known order.

items.stem: The following statement about knowledge representation, constructive memory and forgetting is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "Proactive interference is when new learning disrupts old learning."
items.answer: That is retroactive interference; proactive is old learning disrupting new learning.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (That is retroactive interference; proactive is old learning disrupting new learning.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Elaborative rehearsal helps transfer information to long-term memory. Working memory not only stores information but also manipulates it. Attention transfers information from sensory memory to short-term memory. In the stage model, information passes from sensory memory to short-term memory and then to long-term memory."
(i) Explain the term 'short-term memory', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: A telephone number is forgotten soon after dialling. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Sensory memory has a very small capacity." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The memory system that holds a small amount of information, about seven items, for a brief period unless rehearsed. (ii) Information in short-term memory fades quickly unless it is rehearsed. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Sensory memory has a large capacity but very short duration.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The memory system that holds a small amount of information, about seven items, for a brief period unless rehearsed. (ii) Information in short-term memory fades quickly unless it is rehearsed. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Sensory memory has a large capacity but very short duration.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about information processing model of memory is correct?
items.answer: Information in long-term memory is mainly encoded semantically, in terms of meaning.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: Short-term memory holds about seven items; long-term memory is unlimited. Sensory memory has a large capacity but very short duration. Elaborative rehearsal, which relates new information to old, is better.
options: Maintenance rehearsal is the best way to transfer information to long-term memory.
Information in long-term memory is mainly encoded semantically, in terms of meaning.
Sensory memory has a very small capacity.
Short-term memory has unlimited capacity.

items.stem:
Statement: Students remember more when they think about the meaning of a lesson.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Semantic processing is a deeper level of processing that gives better retention.
items.markingKey: (a) Semantic processing is a deeper level of processing that gives better retention.
options: Semantic processing is a deeper level of processing that gives better retention.
Semantic memory is not tied to the time and place of learning.
Similar learnings interfere with each other.
Procedural memory stores skills that are not easily put into words.
